title: Chain of Peace
subtitle: He declares that the old standoff must end.

trails.title: Trail① The Third Fork in the Road

content.text: Oh, look at you, climbing out of the cave in the allegory, all dusty and dirty like a little savage.
They must have tried to fill your little brain with long preachment, but you should feel lucky because at least they didn't give you a quiz right after that.

branch.text: Oh, that's our expert on absent-mindedness. Yes, we should bear in mind those glory days of yours back in school.
Oh, how modest you are. Looks like you didn't spend all your student days catching tree frogs.

content.text: Try to reach the corners of your mind, if you would, and there you will find another bunch of people standing in front of a stone table.
Yes, those people in gowns, white gowns with gray diamond patterns. One of them was standing on the stairs, gathering all the little vacant eyes to his side. What was he called? Give me a second ...
Teacher, instructor, tutor, educator ... Just titles like that, no names at all. No one gets to write down their names on that banner, after all.
But they have nothing to complain about. You know what they say, "What is reasonable is real; that which is real is reasonable."

They showed you a broad avenue in their teachings, where you could enjoy a sense of security with all the solid ground, convenient automobiles, and warm sunshine. And at the end of the avenue even lies an inspiring mission, to which you are expected to devote your whole life.
There is a distinction between good and bad here, and it's as clear as our innate sense of right and wrong, like a floor of black and white tiles. Any stains on it will be noticed immediately.

But in fact, there exists another path in the woods. It's much less traveled, leading to the unknown darkness which cannot be seen with eyes or proved false. You may even experience indescribable chaos and madness there. This path, however, has an excellent view, and it's one of a kind: the plants are thriving with bursting energy, and the flowers are blooming in a delightful atmosphere.

branch.text: Oh, of course, as you've been on it all the time. But that's exactly why you know how ... inflexible it is. You know that even better than any of those old fellas who have spent decades on it, don't you?
Just because you've been on it doesn't mean you can expect a comfortable journey, darling.
But luckily, there's still one more way you can take. It would be a good choice if you want to enjoy the scenery without getting lost in the darkness.

Oh, that's not an easy choice to make. This grandma must give you a round of applause. I would have even pinned a boutonniere to your suit if I had one. But I have to remind you, those things in there are not easy to deal with. They can drive you insane, and you have to be very careful ...
You've seen the living proof: many were freaked out after they came back, and people had to tie and lock them up; others even dug their own graves.
Oh my, that was a bit over the top. I hope I didn't scare you, darling.
But luckily, there's still one more way you can take. It would be a good choice if you want to enjoy the scenery without getting lost in the darkness.
I'm sure you know that myth.
"You shall take the soul of your love out of the underworld, yet you shall not look back." That's right. You shall pass by the sleeping sirens, yet you shall not make a sound.
The ones with a belief set off. They entered the dark woods barefooted, yet moved so smoothly as if they were walking on the avenue.
They kept their mouths shut and eyes forward. They never turned back, never picked up what was not theirs, never set foot on the forbidden lands, and never looked straight at the sacred greatness.
They showed frugality, patience, and wisdom in the face of hunger and danger.

So the beasts continued to lurk in the shadow, and the ones with a belief passed through the woods safely until the path disappeared along with the direction sign. Then the first one to look back gave an exclamation before being exiled.

content.text: Is it really reasonable to take it?

branch.text: Think about what I just said, "That which is real is reasonable."
Never look back in the woods, darling! If you don't want to be turned into a pillar of salt which can do nothing but wail, then ... NEVER, EVER look back.
Yes, we'd better stay awake, stay calm, stay cautious all the time.

But then there comes the problem: how can anyone ... how can you ignore your love for those thriving plants and blooming flowers? How are you supposed to deal with the unstoppable feeling that overflows like a melody when it is stirred up by the beauty of the scenery?
Of course, you will cry the loudest cry, dance the wildest dance, drink the strongest drink, and vomit all the filth inside you.
After all, there is no need to enter the woods if the soul-stirring scenery is not what you are after, right?

content.text: It doesn't sound like a good way.

branch.text: No, so you'd better let it slip your mind, darling.
Just let it go, and hurry forward. Remember to keep your eyes shut and hold your breath.
When you do so, the scenery will no longer mean anything to you, nor will the fragrance of the flowers. You will get out of the woods and reach where the truth lies.
Is that what you want? Don't worry. We have plenty of time. You may come back at any time and pick another way.

trails.title: Strange Cave
trails.description: A dark, narrow cavern with strange echoes stirring within. It demands a token from you and promises a fable in return.

content.text:
In the fable of the sun,
Sunlight is always rhythmic,
Never to be dampened,
Not to be an umbrella, a ship, or shelter in a downpour,
Not to be a shore, a reef,
To be battered, to be worn down against the waves,
Not to be a cause of capsizing, grounding, lingering, surviving,
Nor to stop moss,
Nor nurture the buds,
To harmonize all colors, but not to pour into each one.
Before the rain veils the sunlight,
Before the clouds swallow the faint shadows,
There remains one last question,
One last answer,
One last way to dissolve conflicts,
One last neutral party,
One last bystander.

items.text: Chain of Peace

In this life there are three kinds of men, 
just as there are three sorts of people who come to the Olympic Games. 
The lowest class is made up of those who come to buy and sell, 
and next above them are those who come to compete.

Best of all, however, are those who come to look on.
 The greatest purification of all is, therefore, science, 
and it is the man who devotes himself to that, the true philosopher, 
who has most effectually released himself from the "wheel of birth." 
                                                      —John Burnet, Early Greek Philosophy

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Before this negotiation begins, I wish to tell an allegory to the two of you.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: A group of people were imprisoned in a cave.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Behind them, there was a fire. Before them was a tall, solid wall.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Their legs and necks were chained and fixed, so they were constrained to look nowhere but to gaze at the wall in front of them.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: When they dropped their eyes, they saw their own body. When they looked up, the flickering light of the fire fell over them, and they only saw the shadows of what was passing behind them.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: No one had lived one day outside the cave. The shadows cast on the wall were all there was to be perceived as reality. They had no knowledge of the real world.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: One day, one of them escaped from the cave, walked into the light, and saw the true world with his own eyes for the first time.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Everything he saw or felt in the cave was nothing more than a mere shadow of the object's true Form.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Our world is a poor one, Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: The phenomenal world is the cave in this allegory, where we are surrounded by shadows or some humble fractions of the truth.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: It is ugly, frivolous, filthy, perishable, subject to decay, and filled with hollow desires and meaningless struggles.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Only the wise can walk out of that cave and see the world as it truly is.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: In that eternal, transcendent world, everything is in its most perfect Form.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I pray that you, Ms. Vertin, the representative of St. Pavlov Foundation, and you, Ms. Arcana, her counterpart of Manus Vindictae, would pay heed to my words.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Everything you've been fighting each other for means no more than some fragments of phenomena to us.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: There's only one thing worth doing.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: That is, to seek higher wisdom, develop one's virtue, and achieve greatness in life.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: We have never set foot on the soil dampened by the "Storm," nor have we ever been involved in the disputes brought by the torrents of time.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I beg you: do not take your conflict in the phenomenal world into the realm of truth.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: For certain.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: It was never my intention to sully the sanctuary of truth.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Then, to prevent a situation like this from happening again ...

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I would like to ask you two to carve your names on these two stone bangles and drip a drop of your blood on each of them.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Once the bracelet is put on, no one will be able to remove it.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: From now on, as long as you're on this island, none of your people will draw blood from one another.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Or the bangle shall draw all the blood from you.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: The peace agreement is so decided.
Arcana stretches out her hand and gently takes a bangle.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I appreciate that.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll sign it.
The leader gives a slight nod.
He looks out from the table and simply strides away.
The bangle feels real in their hands.
It certainly possesses some sort of power to fulfill the bloody pledge.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The peace agreement ...
Someone is approaching.
Yes, she is still here, from the beginning to the end.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Lady Vertin, we meet again.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I wish the best to thy friend.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She's doing "well," thanks to you.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Heh heh. You're most welcome.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Thou shalt quench, for times hath changed.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I would not wish to shed even a drop of arcanist's blood in vain.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But Schneider should be the victim of a merciless bullet?

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Vertin, my pitiful child.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Did you forget?

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: That merciless bullet cameth from a gun never belongen to me.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's Manus Vindictae's purpose to be here?

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Hearken the archaic wisdom.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Just as thou dost.
The stone bangle is hot, almost scalding.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Heh heh ... I am not surprised.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I adore thy visage, Lady Vertin, emotionless in the "Storm."

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Alas ...

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: No man shall bravest the "Storm" and live.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Including thee.
Her words sound as harsh as the winter gale.
An emotion suddenly comes. It's raging like a bush fire but soon gets tamed down.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A wooden box in the Olitiau's base has my name on it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Was that your doing?

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Sadly, it wasn't.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I hope thee findeth the answer satisfactory.
The figure of Arcana disappears in the night.
The stone bangle at the wrist becomes subtly heated.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's burning.
Something is slithering in the woods nearby.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Is that Ms. Arcana?

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Ms. Arcana! Please don't go! Save us!

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: And save art!
Two weary figures run past Vertin.
They are chasing after their leader desperately, as if they are running away from some horrific monsters.
Following them, a petite figure rushes out of the woods.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No. Come back! Come back!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: You ignorant foreigners! I just started introducing vectors and matrices, and that's the most interesting part!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Ah, Vertin!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Great! You always show up at the right time and right place.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Stop the masked people, whatever it takes!
TO BE CONTINUED…
